title: Multi-cloud GPU bursting orchestration and egress-slicing pattern
author: Amina Park
content:
Summary:

This document describes the pattern we use to orchestrate short-duration GPU bursting across multiple cloud providers while minimizing cross-cloud egress costs and preserving latency SLOs for inference jobs. It combines an orchestration policy, an "egress-slicing" traffic shaping model, and IaC modules to make bursts safe, auditable, and revertible.

Goals:
- Allow Redwood workloads to burst into alternate clouds or dedicated partner pools for 1–90 minute windows without losing request-level SLOs.
- Keep cross-account and cross-cloud egress costs predictable and bounded.
- Provide Terraform/IaC primitives and CI/CD hooks so teams can enable bursting safely in their service stacks.
- Provide a minimal on-call runbook for common failures during burst events.

Scope and non-goals:
- Scope: inference-serving traffic (text generation, embeddings, reranking) and offline eval batches that need GPU headroom.
- Non-goals: full multi-cloud data plane replication (we do not attempt to mirror large model checkpoints during a burst).

Key concepts:
- Burst window: a short, policy-defined interval where a service can consume capacity from an alternate provider (usually to avoid throttles or solve regional incidents). Typical window: 5–60 minutes.
- Egress slice: a rate-limited, labeled egress path reserved for burst traffic. Slices are tagged with cost-limits, TTL, and routing priority.
- Cost guardrail: a per-tenant and global budget that gates burst expansion.
- Warm-standby model variants: lightweight model variants (quantized/short-context) used during burst windows to reduce per-token cost and memory.

Architecture overview:
1) Control plane (Redwood scheduler service): evaluates policy and initiates bursts.
2) Routing layer (edge proxies + service mesh): applies egress slicing rules and enforces token-level shaping.
3) Data plane (GPU pools in primary and partner clouds): runs inference tasks; model artifacts are referenced read-only from an immutable object-store snapshot.

Operational pattern — Egress Slicing:
- Each burst-capable service is configured with 2 egress slices: "primary-egress" and "burst-egress".
- "Burst-egress" has an associated egress-budget, cost-tier (spot/commit), and max-pps (packets per second).
- Requests are labeled at the ingress with the workload and customer tags; routing policy uses these tags + cost-remaining to decide whether to forward to burst-egress.

Example policy (natural language):
1) If 95th-percentile latency of primary pool > 2x target for 2 consecutive minutes, attempt small-scale burst (10% of traffic) to partner pool A.
2) If error rate drops and latency improves, grow the burst by +20% every 30s until cost_guardrail or max-burst-percent hit.
3) If cross-cloud egress estimated cost > egress-budget or if error rate increases, immediately retract burst and fallback.

Terraform / IaC patterns:
- Provide a reusable module: redwood-cloud-bursting-slice. Inputs: provider, vpc-id, allowed-subnets, egress-bandwidth-shards, egress-budget-USD, slice-tags. Outputs: route-table attachments, egress-metering labels (via cloud provider tags), and a terraform state locker.

Example minimal module usage (HCL):

```
module "burst_slice_gcp" {
  source = "git::ssh://git@github.com/redwood-inference/infra-modules.git//cloud-bursting-slice?ref=v1.2.0"
  provider = "gcp"
  vpc_id = var.vpc_id
  allowed_subnets = ["subnet-analytics", "subnet-burst"]
  egress_bandwidth_shards = 3
  egress_budget_usd = 150.00
  slice_tags = { team = "search-infra", purpose = "bursting" }
}
```

Note: modules must emit named billing tags used by the cost reporting pipeline. CI/CD pipelines should run a dry-run plan and post the delta to the change approver channel.

CI/CD and image orchestration:
- Build: GPU-sidecar and runtime bundles are built in the same CI job as inference images. Tags: sha, model-shim-hash, kernel-flags.
- Promotion: images must pass the "burst-safety" canary (see test matrix below) before they are allowed onto partner pools.
- Release gate: a policy bot enforces that any change to redwood-cloud-bursting-slice module requires: Terraform plan approval, egress budget signoff by cost-ops, and security scanning for open egress ports.

Burst-safety test matrix (CI):
| Test | Purpose | Threshold |
|------|---------|-----------|
| Load-scaled inference smoke | Ensure model starts under reduced-precision variant | <2% error rate |
| Egress metering/unit test | Validate billing tags emitted | 100% tags present |
| Network failover test | Verify fallback to primary within 8s on simulated egress blackout | 100% success |

Runbook: initiating a controlled burst (procedural steps):
1) Triage root cause of primary-region pressure and confirm burst justification in incident channel.
2) Execute: `terraform apply -var 'enable_burst=true'` in the service's bursting module workspace.
3) Use the scheduler API to start a 10% trial window: `POST /api/v1/scheduler/burst` with body: `{ "service": "svc-name", "percent": 10, "duration": 600 }`.
4) Monitor the "burst-egress" dashboards: egress-cost, p50/p95 latency, packet-drop, and model-error-rate.
5) If metrics remain within thresholds after 5 minutes, expand per policy. Otherwise rollback: `POST /api/v1/scheduler/burst/retract` and set the module flag to `force_disable`.

Troubleshooting quick hits:
- Symptom: burst traffic not reaching partner pool.
  - Check: egress route tables for missing next-hop tags (run `gcloud compute routes list --filter="tags:(burst-ingress)"`).
  - Check: service-mesh egress policy logs for mismatched labels.
- Symptom: unexpected spike in egress estimated cost.
  - Check: cost-ops ledger for untagged flows, verify module emitted billing tags.
- Symptom: model mismatch errors in partner pool.
  - Check: model-shim-hash and runtime bundle tag alignment in the image registry.

SLOs and limits (examples):
- Inference latency SLO during burst: p95 < 250ms for short-context requests.
- Egress budget hard cap: $500/day per service unless explicit escalation.
- Burst growth rate: +20% per 30s; maximum 60% of original traffic.

Ownership and roles:
- Burst controller service: eng-infra/scheduler (primary owner).
- Terraform modules: infra-iac team (owner).
- Cost monitoring and reconciliation: finance-ops/cost-ops.
- Security review and egress policy: security-and-compliance/netsec.

Onboarding checklist for a service enabling bursting:
1) Complete burst-capable runbook template and attach to service page.
2) Add egress tags to CI pipeline and validate tags in dry-run.
3) Confirm warm-standby model variants available in the image registry.
4) Run the burst-safety CI matrix end-to-end.
5) Get egress-budget signoff from cost-ops.

Appendix — Example alert queries:
- PromQL: `sum by (service, slice) (rate(egress_bytes_total[1m])) > 1e8 and service =~ "svc-.*"` (alerts when burst egress exceeds 100MB/s).
- Pager duty rule: page on persistent egress_budget_spend > 90% for 5 minutes.

End of doc.
